reference_direction: Male, medium-low pitch — a magistrate's carrying authority rather than a giant's bass. The stat block deliberately builds him as a mind and a voice rather than a body (Vitality 240 is his floor, Ardency only 348 'and deliberately so'), so the 'Lion' in his epithet should live entirely in command presence, not physical size. Texture is polished and controlled — courtroom-trained, aphoristic, rhetorically balanced (his own line runs sword/law/hand in parallel clauses) — with almost no rasp, since grit would read as a brawler and the card is explicit that he is not one. Pace is measured and weighted, an orator laying clauses down for effect rather than rushing. No accent or dialect is assigned to the Concord bench anywhere on record; play a refined, formal, aristocratic-judicial register that never loosens into slang. Closest comparison: the voice of a senior judge who is also a wartime general — a verdict read from the bench that could just as easily be a battlefield order, its authority coming from precision and resonance rather than volume or bulk.
one_line: A magistrate's measured, resonant authority — not a giant's roar but a judge's verdict-voice, its weight coming from command and magic rather than muscle.
